features.name: Moderation & cases
features.summary: Warn, mute, timeout, kick and ban, each kept as a case with the member's history.
features.lead: The everyday moderation commands. Every action is saved as a case, so a member's history is one command away, and repeated warnings can lead to a timeout.
points: Warn, mute, timeout, kick and ban, from slash commands or right-click.
Every action is a case with the moderator and reason.
/infractions shows one member's whole history.
/infractions has a Purges tab: each purge and what started it, a mod, the auto-kick trap or /clear.
After a set number of warnings, a timeout is offered.
use: Act on a member: `/warn`, `/mute`, `/timeout`, `/kick` or `/ban`, or right-click them › Apps.
See their history: `/infractions`.
Warnings before a timeout is offered: `/warn-settings threshold`; its length: `/warn-settings duration`.
Log actions: `/setup mod-logs`; deleted messages: `/setup cleared-log`.

why.title: Cases, not just actions
why.text: A ban on its own says nothing next month. Keeping each action as a case with its reason is what makes /infractions and appeals possible.

features.name: Automod
features.summary: Removes slurs and your own banned words, with a DM to the sender. Can be switched off per channel or forum.
features.lead: Automod deletes messages with slurs or the server's own banned words, times the sender out for a minute and DMs them why. It can be switched off for one channel, forum or thread, and a forum that's off covers all its posts.
points: Deletes messages with slurs or the server's custom words and DMs the sender.
/automod channel turns it off or on for one channel, forum or thread.
/automod list shows where it's off.
use: Switch it off for a channel or forum: `/automod channel` with filter Off. Posts and threads inside follow it.
See where it's off: `/automod list`.
Turn automod on or off for the whole server, and its DM notices: the dashboard's Settings › Automod.

why.title: Forums follow their parent
why.text: Every forum post is its own thread with its own ID, so exempting the forum alone did nothing for its posts. The filter now checks the post's forum too.

features.name: Softban & appeals
features.summary: Locks a member into one channel where they can appeal, instead of banning them.
features.lead: A softban takes a member's roles and leaves them one channel. After a wait they can open an appeal ticket, and staff approve or deny it with a button.
points: The member keeps their place but sees only the softban lobby.
After a wait, an Appeal button opens a private ticket.
Staff approve or deny from the ticket; approving gives their roles back.
Softbans survive leaving and rejoining.
Evidence from an approved /request-softban is copied to a locked #evidence channel in the staff server, and the softban links to it.
use: Softban: `/softban`. Members without the permission can `/request-softban`.
Set the softban role and lobby channel: `/setup softban`.
Store softban evidence: `/setup evidence` in the staff server makes the locked channel (optional view-role reads it).
Remove a stored post: `/evidence remove` with its EV ID (deleting the post by hand works too).
Decide an appeal: the buttons in the ticket, or `/appeal approve` and `/appeal deny`.
Lift it early: `/unsoftban`.

why.title: A way back
why.text: A ban gives no room to explain. Keeping the member in one channel lets them appeal without DMs, and keeps the decision in front of staff.

features.name: Account age gate
features.summary: Accounts younger than 30 days are timed out on join and see only one channel until they're 30 days old.
features.lead: In servers that turn it on, a new account sees only one channel and can't chat until it's 30 days old. A 5-day-old account waits 25 days. The join card shows until when, and Mark safe lets someone in early.
points: Off until a server turns it on. The 30 days are fixed.
Timed out, and only the info channel is visible until day 30.
The join card shows until when, and Mark safe lets them in early.
One info card in the channel you pick explains the rule.
use: Turn it on: `/setup account-age enabled:True info-channel:#new-accounts`, or the dashboard's Server › Logging. The bot needs Timeout Members, Manage Roles and Manage Channels.
Let someone in early: Mark safe on their join card. It's posted to the mod log.
Turn it off: `/setup account-age enabled:False`. The new account role is deleted; running timeouts end on their own dates.

why.title: Longer than Discord allows
why.text: Discord stops a timeout at 28 days, so an account 0 or 1 day old gets 28 days and the bot adds the rest. It only extends a timeout that is still its own.

why.title: No Timeout 1 h on a held member
why.text: That button would replace a timeout of weeks with one of an hour, so it's left off the card while someone waits.

why.title: Join role waits
why.text: A role allowed into a channel would beat the hide, so the server's join role is given when the wait ends.

features.name: Private VCs
features.summary: Join one channel to get your own voice room, with a menu to lock, rename or invite.
features.lead: Joining the "Join to create" channel makes a voice room for you and moves you in. Menus in the room let you lock, hide, rename and limit it, or kick and block people.
points: Join one channel, get your own room.
Lock, hide, rename and set a user limit from menus in the room.
Kick or block people; hand the room to someone else.
The room is deleted when everyone has left.
use: Set it up: `/setup voice` with the categories and your mod role.
Use it: join "Join to create", then use the menu in your room.
rules: The panel is usable by the room's owner, admins and the configured mod role only; being in the room grants nothing.
The mod role gets a full-bypass overwrite on every room: it sees and joins locked and hidden rooms.
The owner, bots, admins and mods can't be kicked or blocked.
Blocks are channel permission overwrites, so they disappear when the room is deleted.
Kick counts are kept in memory: cleared when the room is deleted, reset when the bot restarts.
The muted role can't see or join "Join to create", is silently disconnected if it lands there anyway, and can see but never connect to rooms; that deny is re-applied on unlock and show.
A room is deleted the moment its owner leaves, or when it becomes empty; deleting one by hand removes its record too.
`/setup voice` refuses to run until `/setup mute-role` has stored a mute role that still exists, and re-running it replaces the config and deletes the old join channel.

why.title: Images live in the database
why.text: Linked images can break or expire. Uploaded images are kept with the rest of the bot's data, apart from the command list so it stays small, and the bot attaches them to its reply.

features.name: Cross-server calls
features.summary: Chat with another server through a call channel, matched at random.
features.lead: Pick a call channel and run `taxx!call`. syntaxx matches you with another server, and messages cross over both ways until someone hangs up or the call goes quiet.
points: Pairs your call channel with another server's at random.
The waiting server accepts or declines, unless it turned Require Accept off.
Up to 3 servers in one call, shown by colour labels, not names.
Every relayed message passes the word filter.
Mods on the other side can trace or time out a sender.
use: Pick the channel: `taxx!setupcallchannel #calls`, or the dashboard's Settings › Calls. Require Accept and the idle timeout are there too.
Let a role call and hang up: `taxx!perms allow call -r <role>`, then the same for `hangup`.
Call: `taxx!call`. Stop waiting: `taxx!call cancel`. Join a call already going: `taxx!call mashup`. End: `taxx!hangup`.
Moderate by replying to a relayed message: `taxx!callinfo` tells you who sent it, `taxx!calltimeout <minutes> [reason]` stops them relaying.

why.title: Labels, not server names
why.text: In a 3-server call the others only see 🔴 Server A, 🔵 Server B and 🟢 Server C, so an offensive server name can't reach anyone.

why.title: Moderation by reply
why.text: You can only trace or time out someone who actually sent into your channel, so no one can be targeted by a typed ID.

why.title: The filter always runs
why.text: Relayed text passes the word filter even when a server has automod off, because it lands in someone else's server.

arrived.what: Accept and Decline work again, so Require Accept is back.
arrived.label: 14 Nov 2026
